# Code of Conduct

## The point

This code of conduct is mainly to guide contributors and community members, not really enforce rules.  
The point is so we can all have a safe and welcoming environment without harassment, discrimination, or any other negative behavior.

You should primarily follow:
- Treat everyone with respect and kindness
- Don't degrade anyone or any space, even if you disagree with them
- Conflict is inevitable and should be productive
- You should be Good, not just Not Bad

## Treat everyone with respect and kindness

- Be friendly and welcoming to others
- Do not say anything insulting, demeaning, hateful or threatening to anyone
- Do not discriminate against people in your word or actions.

## Don't degrade shared spaces

Any shared spaces, whether it be a github issue or even a Discord server, in general you should not degrade the space or the people in it. This applies to anything relating to Hackflare as well.  
Keep things like issues and pull requests productive and on-topic too.

## Conflict is inevitable and should be productive

- When someone disagrees with you, try to understand what they thing and why
- Do not escalate conflicts even if you are provoked, instead try to de-escalate the situation
- Do not rally sentiment against others
- Always assume that people are acting in good faith, even if you disagree with them
- Be patient, people are busy and need to understand your point of view when answering or replying to you.
- Think about how your words may be interpreted before you say them, and if they may be misinterpreted, clarify your point of view.
- Take a moment to think before you speak, espically if you are in a heated discussion.

## You should be Good, not just Not Bad

You shouln't think of how to stay within the rules, but rather just be good in general. If you are unsure if something is appropriate, ask yourself if it is respectful and productive. If it is not, then it is probably not appropriate.

## Conclusion

This is pretty open-ended but the point is to have a safe and welcoming environment for everyone.  
There is nothing wrong with showing your point of view, but you should do it in a respectful and productive way.
